data.narrative:
General Matter is a Series A nuclear energy company founded by Scott Nolan and Lee Robinson that has raised $50M+. Valuation was triangulated against a comp universe of 11 peers (3 public, 8 private) in the nuclear energy sector at same and adjacent stages, including Fuse Energy, Valar Atomics, and Nano Nuclear Energy.

Two methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $50M total raised as a proxy base value and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement, yielding $100M. Peer-median analysis draws from three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables with valuations of $200M (Fuse Energy, Series A), $808M (Nano Nuclear Energy, Seed), and $6.0B (Valar Atomics, Series B), producing a median implied value of $808M and a range of $200M to $6.0B.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $85M to $929M, with a median of $454M. The wide spread reflects material stage and maturity heterogeneity within the peer set: Valar Atomics' $6.0B Series B valuation elevates the upper bound significantly, while Fuse Energy's $200M Series A comparable anchors the lower bound. Key uncertainties center on General Matter's technology differentiation within the crowded advanced nuclear sector and the sustainability of recent valuation inflation evident in later-stage peers.
